name: Old Laptop
description: Decommissioned notebook or netbook with dead motherboard or cracked hinge.
warnings: Li-ion battery pack: Never puncture, bend, or short-circuit terminals.
Discharge residual inverter or power supply caps before touching board traces.
Wear eye protection when prying plastic snaps and display bezels.

name: Old Smartphone
description: Obsolete Android or iOS phone with broken battery or outdated OS.
warnings: Lithium-polymer pouch battery can swell or catch fire if punctured.
Use heat gun or hair dryer on low heat to soften adhesive without blistering cells.

name: Broken USB Keyboard
description: Membrane or mechanical keyboard with non-functional keys or severed cord.
warnings: Handle circuit traces gently; flexible membrane ribbon cables tear easily.
Watch out for small metal spring clips popping loose during disassembly.

name: Old Wi-Fi Router
description: Retired ISP gateway or 2.4GHz Wi-Fi access point.
warnings: Wall adapter must be unplugged from mains AC for at least 5 minutes before opening casing.
Internal electrolytic filtering capacitors may retain high voltage.

name: Dead Desktop PC (SMPS)
description: Defective ATX Desktop Power Supply unit and chassis.
warnings: DANGER: Large primary 400V capacitors can hold lethal charge even days after unplugging! Discharge with insulated high-wattage resistor before touching.
Do NOT plug SMPS directly into mains with open housing.

name: Discarded CD/DVD Drive
description: Obsolete optical drive from desktop computer or external enclosure.
warnings: Avoid direct line-of-sight exposure to laser diode when powered up.
Greased mechanical worm gears can attract dust; degrease before clean reuse.
